record.paper_title: Conferences WORDS, years 1997-2017: Open Problems and Conjectures
record.original_question: By applying prefix-suffix completion, can we construct words that avoid cubes, and every word containing squares?

evidence.quote: By applying prefix-suffix completion, can we construct words that avoid cubes, and every word containing squares?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Sigma$ be a finite alphabet and $\Sigma^*$ the free monoid of finite words over $\Sigma$. For words $u,v \in \Sigma^*$, write $u \Rightarrow_{ps} v$ (one step of prefix-suffix square completion) if either:
- there exist $x,y \in \Sigma^*$ with $y$ nonempty such that $u$ has the suffix $yx$ where $u = \alpha y x$ for some $\alpha$, and $v = u\,y$ (so that $v$ ends in the square $yy$); or, symmetrically,
- $u$ has a prefix $xy$ with $y$ nonempty, and $v = y\,u$ (so that $v$ begins with the square $yy$).

Equivalently, the suffix square completion appends a nonempty word $y$ to $u$ whenever $u$ already ends with $y$, producing a new suffix $yy$; and the prefix square completion is its mirror image.

Let $\Rightarrow_{ps}^*$ denote the reflexive transitive closure of this relation. An infinite word $w \in \Sigma^\omega$ is said to be generated by prefix-suffix square completion (from a finite seed $w_0$) if there is an infinite sequence $w_0 \Rightarrow_{ps} w_1 \Rightarrow_{ps} w_2 \Rightarrow_{ps} \cdots$ whose limit is $w$.

A word is cube-free if it contains no factor of the form $xxx$ with $x$ nonempty. Note that, by construction, every word produced by a nontrivial prefix-suffix square completion step contains a square.

Question: Does there exist a finite alphabet $\Sigma$ and a finite seed word $w_0 \in \Sigma^*$ from which prefix-suffix square completion generates an infinite word $w$ such that:
(i) $w$ is cube-free, and
(ii) every finite factor of $w$ contains at least one square?

More generally, characterize the infinite words obtainable by iterated prefix-suffix square completion that simultaneously avoid cubes and have the property that every sufficiently long factor contains a square.
artifact.status_search_result: Search results confirm prefix-suffix square completion has been studied (e.g., the original paper by Ito, Leupold, Manea, Mitrana and follow-ups on prefix/suffix-square-free words and prefix-suffix square reduction). It is known that infinite cube-free words can be generated by such operations. However, no source located explicitly resolves the combined requirement of avoiding cubes while ensuring every factor contains a square via prefix-suffix square completion. The status therefore appears unresolved based on the available evidence.

status_evidence.title: Prefix-Suffix Square Completion
status_evidence.snippet: Defines the prefix-suffix square completion operation and studies which words can be generated.
status_evidence.claim: Establishes the framework but does not settle the combined cube-avoidance / square-containing question.

status_evidence.title: On Prefix/Suffix-Square Free Words
status_evidence.snippet: Studies words avoiding prefix/suffix squares; related but distinct setting.
status_evidence.claim: Related work, does not directly resolve the question.

status_evidence.title: Prefix–suffix square reduction
status_evidence.snippet: Considers the inverse operation of prefix-suffix square completion.
status_evidence.claim: Companion line of research; does not resolve the open problem.
